questions.q: What calculates transaction tax on a Payables invoice?
options: A rule built directly into the Payables module
Oracle Fusion Tax, a shared engine used across Payables, Receivables, and other modules
questions.explain: Transaction tax is calculated by the shared Oracle Fusion Tax engine, not by Payables-specific logic.

options: A type of invoice approval rule
A piece of invoice information, like ship-to location or product category, that the tax engine uses to decide which tax and rate applies
questions.explain: Tax determinants are the data points on the invoice header/line the tax engine uses to calculate applicable tax.

questions.q: What happens to an invoice's total amount when self-assessed tax applies?
options: It stays the same — the supplier is still paid exactly what they billed
It increases by the tax amount, same as ordinary transaction tax
It is reduced by the tax amount
questions.explain: Self-assessed tax doesn't change what's paid to the supplier; it's recorded as a liability the purchaser owes directly, via offsetting distributions.

questions.q: What is the key difference between transaction tax and withholding tax?
options: They are two names for exactly the same thing
Withholding tax only applies to credit memos
Transaction tax is tax on the transaction itself (like sales tax); withholding tax is withheld from what's paid to the supplier and remitted on their behalf
questions.explain: Transaction tax taxes the transaction; withholding tax is an amount withheld from the supplier's payment itself.

questions.q: In the Solara Packaging example with a $1,000 invoice and 8% ordinary sales tax, how much does Solara actually get paid?
questions.explain: With ordinary (non-self-assessed) transaction tax, the tax is added to the invoice total, and the supplier is paid the full $1,080.
